output.summary: KEP-2382 re-introduces exec-based SecretGenerators in Kustomize, which were removed in v2, behind explicit safeguards. The KEP is implementable at alpha stage.
output.rationale: Kustomize removed exec secret generation in v2 because publishers of a kustomization.yaml could run arbitrary commands on users' machines. Users still want Secrets produced by tools they already run, for example to decrypt or fetch secrets without writing them to disk. The proposal re-adds exec generators but gates them: they are off unless a flag enables them, and executables must sit in a flag-defined path that is empty by default.

alternatives.option: Keep exec generators removed, as in kustomize v2
alternatives.why_not: The KEP targets a commonly requested use case: users want Secrets generated by commands without them appearing decrypted on disk. The sources do not record any further rejection of this option.

alternatives.option: Allow any executable on the PATH to be run
alternatives.why_not: The proposal restricts executables to flag-defined paths that are empty by default, so users must install or symlink executables there. The sources do not describe a PATH-based alternative in more detail.

alternatives.option: Support an ecosystem of user-shared plugins
alternatives.why_not: This is listed as a non-goal: the design targets an organization-configured set of tools, not a marketplace of shared plugins.

evidence.quote: Re-introduce `exec` SecretGenerators, but with the following safeguards in place to address security concerns.
Plugins must be explicitly enabled with a flag. If it is not enabled and is used, Kustomize will exit 1 without running exec.
Executables are restricted to flag defined paths - defaulted a location that is empty by default.
The ability to generate Secrets using `exec` was removed in kustomize v2 because of security concerns
Support an ecosystem of users (i.e. not centralized within a single organization) authoring plugins and sharing them with one another.
